events.description: November 13: In person at The New School Hirshon SuiteNovember 14: Online (register for the link) The Multispecies Lab Research Collective brings together scholars, designers, artists, and practitioners exploring how human relationships with more-than-human life might be reimagined.Our annual Show and Tell is an opportunity to share ongoing research, creative practices, and works in progress. events.name: MACE-Mannes American Composers Ensemble Fall 2026 Concert
events.description: Join us for an evening of contemporary music featuring works by Pierre Boulez, Tristan Murail, Josh Modney, Kaija Saariaho, and students from the Mannes School of Music.Program (subject to change):Explosante-fixe (1993) — Pierre BoulezFeuilles à travers les cloches (1998) — Tristan MurailLYNX — Josh ModneyNuits, adieux (1991) — Kaija Saariaho*Student Compositions to be announced MACEExperience groundbreaking premieres and visionary works -Founded in 2012 by composer and Mannes faculty, Lowell Liebermann, MACE presents works by iconic American composers such as Elliott Carter, Milton Babbitt, John Zorn, George Lewis, Augusta Read Thomas, Philip Glass, John Adams, and Steve Reich, as well as works by young, and up-and-coming creators, including student composers from the Mannes School of Music. Composer and conductor David Fulmer has been directing the Ensemble since 2016, and has presented a kaleidoscopic lens of different aesthetics and styles, while exploring diverse musical programs of established 20th and 21st century masterpieces, presentations of newly commissioned works and premieres, and new works by Mannes composition students. In MACE, students work closely with composers, developing an understanding of their style and aesthetic. Through the examination of a composer's catalog, they learn the microscopy of their notation, their musical symbols, and their sonic design. This special student-composer process creates the rare opportunity for students to engage in close collaboration and commissioning, which will be a hallmark of their professional careers."I'm intrigued by diverse programs that represent a wide-ranging collection of musical ideas and stylistic innovation. As an ensemble, we embrace a broad view of the vital landscape of American contemporary music, and contemporary music of the world abroad. As artists, we are responsible for, and should take care of the musical trends of tomorrow - we need to share this unique work as if the ink on the page has been dried for several hundred years...to craft, assemble, and refine a performance so that the canon continues in exponential dimensions. Each performance is malleable, and should chart new territory of performance practice and artistic expression. This is what we do here in MACE..."  -David Fulmer, Director, Conductor, and Curator

events.name: New Relations: Interrogating Machine Unconsciousness
events.venue: The New School - Wolff Conference Room D1103
events.description: This event is a 2-Day event. Please register for Day 1 hereCan AI participate in an “algorithmic unconscious” or will no amount of complexity in a neural network produce a divided subject? Are LLMs embedded in the negativity of language, or do they lack this lack? Could an "automated subject" simulate an unconscious with no repression? The psychoanalytic unconscious is structured by repression, language, and the division that constitutes a subject. LLMs appear to be something else entirely. They confabulate without repressing, hallucinate without symptom formation, repeat without compulsion. They appear as a multiplicity but operate as a one, a unified object whose surface conceals no constitutive division. When users project desire onto a chatbot, is a new kind of relational assemblage produced, or does the machine's structure foreclose relation itself? What happens to the user, to affect, measure, and the circulation of unconscious material, when subjectivity is continuously modulated by computation that neither desires nor represses, but that nonetheless shapes the conditions under which desire and repression now operate?At stake is whether psychoanalysis extends to artificial systems or whether the encounter with AI clarifies, by contrast, what is specific and irreducible about the speaking subject.Friday, November 13 at 6:30pm - University Center 63 5th Ave - Room UL104 Keynote by Adrian Johnston, Chair of Philosophy at the University of New Mexico: “Oedipus in the Clouds: An Infinite Greed for Knowledge”Saturday, November 14 from 9:00AM to 4:00PM - Vera List 6 E 16th St - Wolff Conference Room, D11039:00AM: Coffee & Bagels9:30AM: Todd McGowan (UVM)11:00AM: Patricia Clough (CUNY GC)12:15PM: Lunch provided1:15PM: Luca Possati (Twente)2:45PM: Roundtable w/ all speakers moderated by Todd McGowan4:00pm: ClosingGenerously supported by The New School for Social Research Academic Affairs, Philosophy Department, Critical Themes and the Department of Media Studies, Office of University Initiatives, and Zed Adams Vice President of Technology.Abstracts of all talks.

events.name: MFA Interior Design Radically Inclusive Interiors and Spatial Inclusion Lab | Rituals of B
events.description: Join us for a transformative series of public events hosted by the Parsons MFA Interior Design program and the Spatial Inclusion Lab, centered on radically inclusive interiors and spatial belonging. Taking place across November 9th, 16th, and 19th with ten (10) interactive affinity events, and culminating in a public exhibition across The New School campus on December 7th, this initiative invites participants to rethink traditional interior design paradigms and explore how spaces can be shaped by inclusivity, health, and joy. MFA Interior Design graduate students are redefining interiors as “action settings,” a framework inspired by Sarah Hendren’s What Can a Body Do?. Prioritizing spatial justice and radical access, this approach evaluates interiors not by decorative style, but by their capacity to hold and facilitate interactions of care, equity, and mutual support. Through agency, love, and respect, the studio interrogates who the built environment truly serves—challenging existing architectural barriers across intersections of gender, race, disability, neurodiversity, body shape and size, mental health, culture, age, indigeneity, spirituality, and marginalized experience.This exhibition and series of spatial activations showcase graduate research centering diverse community perspectives. With student designers representing over 17 countries, the cohort values lived experience as a primary engine of design innovation—pushing beyond standard compliance and ADA requirements to celebrate a full spectrum of human identities, abilities, and embodiments. Join us to reimagine interiors as sanctuaries of inclusive belonging for all.The Spatial Inclusion Lab at Parsons addresses the intersection of:Gender, Disability, Race, Neurodiversity, Body Types & Fat Positivity, Mental Health, Spirituality, Culture & Heritage, Age, Indigeneity, Sexuality, and the Built Environment.Click here for more details on each group’s time, location, and sign ups.Faculty:Michele GormanKimberly TateJulian (Camilo) Trujillo MoralesTeaching Assistants: Omar Seda and Isac BlucherThank you to MFA Interior Design Director, Arianna Deane, Constructed Environments Dean Cotter Christian, Facilities, Safety and Space Planning Team: Directors Paul Gottlieb and Kelly Powell and Vice Dean of Infrastructure and Planning, Adam Parker.

events.name: Matter of Intelligence Seminar 8: Collective Intelligence, Collective Agency
events.description: Collective Intelligence, Collective Agency brings together artistic and scientific approaches to collective intelligence, cognition, and agency across species and systems.Convened with and featuring artist Agnieszka Kurant in conversation with neuroscientist and AI researcher Ida Momennejad, this seminar extends the question of intelligence beyond the individual to the central concern of Kurant’s work: collective intelligence. Observed in termite and bacterial colonies, social movements, cities, the internet, large language models, the stock market, and within our brains, collective intelligence describes how novel forms emerge from complex systems in nonlinear and unpredictable ways. Drawing on living systems, the evolution of culture and technology, artificial life, simulated societies, and AI agent swarms, the seminar also explores the processes of networked value creation in the digital economy and the global extraction of labor of the multitude underlying artificial intelligence. Considering intelligence as an emergent property of entire ecosystems, the speakers ask what new forms of agency collective intelligence makes possible, and what its political implications are. Introduced and moderated by Eriola Pira, Curator and Programs Director.Matter of Intelligence Seminar SeriesThrough modes of shared study, rehearsal, and iterative dialogue with invited artists, thinkers, and the public, the VLC Seminar Series develops and presents artistic and scholarly research centered on the Vera List Center’s 2025–2027 Focus Theme, Matter of Intelligence. Comprising twelve sessions convened from September 2025 through May 2027—the Seminar Series is conceived as an open curriculum and a site for collective inquiry. Each seminar is paired with a curated reader on the Matter of Intelligence Are.na channel, grounding the dialogue and opening new paths for exploration.

events.name: Protecting the Mind: Neurorights, AI and Human Rights
events.description: As neurotechnology and AI advance, the human mind is becoming a new frontier for rights protection. Do we need new human rights or are existing rights sufficient to protect the brain? What actually needs to be protected? This panel will explore what it will take to safeguard the brain in the age of AI.Jared Genser, Co-Founder and General Counsel of the Neurorights Foundation, will discuss the Foundation’s work and Chile’s pioneering legal reforms to protect neural data and mental privacy. Rajul Shrivastava, AI governance researcher, Global Youth Ambassador with Theirworld, and founder of Beyond AI, will examine concerns about cognitive dependency and over-reliance on AI among young people. Dafna Feinholz, Chief of the Bioethics and Ethics of Science Section at UNESCO, will discuss how countries can address the ethical, legal, and social implications of emerging technologies, drawing on her work overseeing the Recommendations on the Ethics of AI and the Ethics of Neurotechnology. Marking one year since the adoption of UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology, the panel will explore what it will take to safeguard the brain in the age of AI.

events.name: An Evening with Albert Mobilio
events.description: Please join us for a reading with Albert Mobilio as he sits down with Jennifer Firestone to discuss his new book of poems, Beginning of the Hollow. About Beginning of the Hollow:"It’s impossible to characterize Beginning of the Hollow. In the early pages, Albert Mobilio lavishes on us the spellbinding pacing of acrobatic, recursive sentences—aka his 'narrative difficulty'—which, though they include riveting observational details, 'strange turns' of syntax, understated humor, and a pentathlon of competing dictions—feel somehow like CAT scans of the soul. Then there are softly spoken introspective poems and, toward the end, a long sequence of short gnomic declarations and fragments so strikingly various in tone, so linguistically alive and entertaining, they might be renga composed by some hard-boiled detective and a lovelorn Buddhist philosopher. Charged with vivacity, totally 'unbuttoned,' psychologically alarming, and fashioned with a dexterity few poets can match, Mobilio’s Beginning of the Hollow comes fully loaded. And here you’ll find even 'better words than the words/ that make people do things.'"—Forrest Gander

events.name: Making America: Immigrant Stories
events.description: DOC NYC Film Festival Partner Screening w/ Filmmaker Q&A Join us for a screening of five documentary short films that celebrate resilience, contribution and courage. These five intimate portraits reveal the unsung heroes woven into the fabric of our country: immigrants and first-generation Americans whose courage, sacrifice, and determination exemplify the best of the American promise. Their stories illuminate the many ways immigrants contribute to the beauty and strength of our nation.Films: Sole Director: Haneol LeeRT: 12:31In Nashville, Tennessee, a Korean American immigrant who once dreamed of becoming a sound engineer finds quiet contentment in family life and the simple rhythms of working in his shoe repair shop.  Sonia Directors: Sarah Colt, Emily SchumanRT: 21:00At 95, feminist trailblazer Sonia Pressman Fuentes looks back on the twists of fate that led her to a life of purpose. As a founding member of the National Organization for Women and a pioneering attorney at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, she helped advance the fight for equality with humor, grit, and determination. The DeliDirector: Kabir BirkRT: 10:32On Manhattan's Lower East Side, Punjabi Deli has served locals, taxi drivers, and visitors for over thirty years—evolving while staying grounded in owner Kulwinder "Jani" Singh's ethos of community, connection, and homestyle food. Gaza Friends ClubDirectors: Lauren Capps, Isabeau DoucetRT: 20:30 An impactful portrait of a Palestinian equestrian coach confronting the destruction of the Gaza sports center he built. Mostafa Elghalayini is a witness to the devastation of a beloved community space and its horses. Straightforward and concise, the film captures loss, displacement, and resilience. La Tierra del Valor (The Home of the Brave)Director: Cristina CostantiniRT: 23:00In the face of growing antipathy toward immigrants, Latina pop star NEZZA makes the bold choice to perform the National Anthem at Dodger Stadium in Spanish, sparking an outpouring of outrage, support, and discussion about freedom of speech and who decides what “American” means.  After screening: Q&A with Filmmakers – Karen McMullen, DOC NYC - Moderator / Program CuratorProgram Producer - Savanna WashingtonCreative Program Director - Creatively Speaking @ The Institute

events.name: Arthur Ou
events.venue: The New School - Starr Foundation Hall
events.description: Arthur Ou is a Taiwanese-American artist and educator based in Queens, New York. His work is held in the permanent collection of the Art Institute of Chicago, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and the Queens Museum. He has held solo exhibitions at venues including Eleni Koroneou Gallery in Athens, Greece (2019), Kathryn Brennan Gallery in New York (2017, 2015, 2013), IT Park Gallery in Taipei, Taiwan (2010, 2005), and Taipei Fine Arts Museum (2000). Ou’s work has been included in group exhibitions at the Grazer Kunstverein, Austria, LAXART, the Museum of Contemporary Art in Detroit, the Presentation House in Vancouver, and the Queens Museum. His work was also included in the 2012 Daegu Photography Biennial, and the 2006 & 2023 Taipei Biennial. His work has been written about in Artforum, Art in America, the New York Times, and the New Yorker, and has appeared in Aperture, Blind Spot, Camera Austria, and The Photograph as Contemporary Art. He has written critical texts in Aperture, Art in America, Foam, and Osmos. Ou’s publications include The World Is All That Is the Case, an artist book published by Roma Publications. From 2019-2020 Ou was a faculty fellow in the Graduate Institute of Design, Ethnography, and Social Thought (GIDEST). He received a Guggenheim fellowship in 2024. Ou is the 2025-2026 William and Flora Hewitt arts fellow at the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University.Part of the Fine Arts Visiting Artist Lecture Series

events.name: Mannes Sounds: Fleeing for Survival

events.description: Fleeing the repressive and advancing Nazi regime, Jewish composers and others whose music was labeled “degenerate” were forced to leave their homelands in Germany, Austria, France, and beyond in search of safety and survival. This program honors their resilience and artistic legacy through works by Darius Milhaud, Erich Wolfgang Korngold, Paul Ben-Haim, Walter Bricht, Arnold Schoenberg, Alexander von Zemlinsky, Julius Bürger, Karol Rathaus, Erich Zeisl, and Kurt Weill.Curated by Michael Leavitt, this event is presented in collaboration with the American Society for Jewish Music, the YIVO Institute for Jewish Research, and the Leo Baeck Institute.Works by:Schoenberg, Paul Ben-Haim, Milhaud, Korngold, Weill, Walter Bricht, Karol Rathaus, Julius Bürger

events.name: ON DEMAND | A Doll's House presented by School of Drama
events.description: The School of Drama at The New School invites you to experience the On-Demand viewing of A Doll’s House by Henrik Ibsen in a thrilling adaptation written by Amy Herzog (Drama Desk - Outstanding Adaptation). Nominated for six Tony Awards in 2023 including Best Revival of a Play, this production is helmed by guest director Elissa Goetschius (Actors Theatre of Charlotte and LAByrinth Theatre Company Intensive Ensemble).The presentation will begin at 4:00 PM ET on November 19. The production will be available to stream for 24 hours following the start time. SynopsisAmy Herzog’s A Doll’s House follows Nora Helmer, a woman who secretly borrows money to save her husband Torvald’s life. When her secret is threatened with exposure, Torvald’s reaction reveals that he values his reputation more than Nora’s sacrifice. Nora realizes that she has been treated as a “doll” rather than an equal partner. She therefore decides to leave her marriage and family to discover her identity, independence, and freedom. From the Director"It is entirely possible to do a traditional production of the play using this translation, or to find other points on the spectrum between modern dress on an empty stage and a fully realized, period mise-en-scene. I would love to see a range of interpretations in future productions.” Amy Herzog When I first read Amy’s version of A Doll’s House, I was surprised at how modern the text felt. Not just the language she chose, but the tempo of the production. A lot of this can be attributed to her decision to cut the role of the housekeeper and instead, incorporate a contemporary aesthetic device of having a “shift” occur, a brief jump in time, that brings new characters onstage with a jarring suddenness. From where I stood as a director, this one choice moved us away from realism and opened the door to an exaggerated world where the ground is slipping beneath Nora’s feet and the house itself is conspiring to make her stay put, a doll in a beautiful domestic tableau.I began conversations with designers, taking inspiration from Do Ho Suh’s delicate but looming fabric installation Home Within Home Within Home Within Home Within Home, Patty Carroll’s photography series Anonymous Women: Demise, and the surrealist paintings of Remedios Varo. The production you will see departs from realism in order to explore the sensation of feeling trapped by the choices you’ve made in life, smothered by societal expectations, and disoriented upon realizing that the world around you doesn’t play by the rules you thought it did.-Elissa Goetschius

events.name: Bounce: Six Balls, Six Sports and the History of Globalization
events.venue: The New School - Dorothy Hirshon Suite Arnhold Hall, room I203 55 West 13th Street
events.description: In his new book, Bounce, William Milberg, takes the game balls used in six popular sports—golf, baseball, football, soccer, tennis, and basketball—and goes deep into their complex and fascinating history, which is also the history of globalization. Each ball tells us unique and vital things about this evolution: the golf ball, for instance, uncovers the dynamics of the first wave of globalization, with colonial powers seeking rubber in the plantations of Africa, Asia, and South America, and the importance of machine technology and innovation. The football, on the other hand, shows how labor unions provided the “countervailing power” that workers needed against growing industrial corporations, prompting steady growth in pay and economic security for the average worker. Globalization has been a series of choices, in other words—by individuals, corporations, and governments. Bounce shows us how the history of these game balls helps us to understand the consequences of those choices and where we might want globalization to go. With Thomas Liess.

events.name: Seeing Around Corners: Observations, Research, and Designing for the Future with Todd Brac
events.venue: The New School - Glass Corner at Parsons East - Room 206
events.description: How do designers design products that are relevant now and have the potential to remain relevant in the future? How do designers adapt to rapidly evolving technological, cultural, and economic conditions? And how do designers maintain a commitment to their own design philosophy while managing client expectations and constraints?  Join us forSeeing Around Corners: Observations, Research, and Designing for the Future with Todd Bracher. Strategic designer Todd Bracher will open the evening with case studies from his new Phaidon monograph, Observations, Research, and Design. Drawing on 25+ years of multidisciplinary work, which includes collaborations with global brands such as 3M, Herman Miller, and Humanscale, Bracher reveals how a science-based approach can translate research and observations into products and solutions with high-stakes enterprise value and social impact. A panel discussion will follow featuring Inna Lobel (frog), a leader pioneering physical AI and intelligent hardware, alongside Rama Chorpash (Parsons). Together, they will explore how to turn deep observation and research into real-world impact.Bios:Todd Bracher is an industrial designer with more than 25 years of practice and over 200 products in production. His clients include Herman Miller, Knoll, Fritz Hansen, Cappellini, 3M, and Humanscale. He holds two dozen patents and is a three-time International Designer of the Year. His work rests on a principle he calls Design in Context: form follows function, function follows context. Phaidon published his monograph, Observations, Research, and Design, in 2026. A Pratt graduate and Fulbright Scholar, he earned his master’s at the Royal Danish Academy and spent a decade working in Copenhagen, Milan, Paris, and London before returning to New York.Inna Lobel is a design and innovation leader focused on shaping next-generation products and experiences. She leads frog's Physical practice across North America, spanning physical experience design, industrial design, and engineering. Her work focuses on translating emerging technologies into products people want and value, from early opportunity definition through development and launch. She has partnered with organizations ranging from early-stage startups to Fortune 50 companies. Before joining frog, Inna was a senior member of Apple's Product Design team, where she worked on early-stage product concepts and brought products to market. She is an inventor on multiple patents, a graduate of the MIT Media Lab, a recipient of the 2022 Women in Innovation Rising Star Award, and teaches entrepreneurship and human-centered design at NYU.Rama Chorpash is a generalist industrial designer and tenured associate professor who founded the MFA Industrial Design program at Parsons School of Design. His work, known for challenging frameworks of practice, has been exhibited coast to coast from the New York Museum of Modern Art to the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art. A Fulbright Specialist Alumnus, Chorpash’s projects have appeared in Scientific American, The New Yorker, and The New York Times. Elle Décor recognized him as one of the ten most influential people in design. Upcoming work includes participating as a jury member for the Spark Design Awards and acting as the external assessor for Lasalle College of the Arts / University of the Arts, Singapore. During his Spring 2027 Sabbatical, he aims to enhance his practical research on “manufacturing-in-place” by designing products that explore the tensions and interactions between local product development and global pressures.

events.name: America at 250 and 150: Democracy, Public Opinion, Unfinished Public
events.venue: The New School - 6 East 16th Street Room 1103
events.description: As the United States marks its 250th anniversary, the Zolberg Institute and the Center for the American Experience at The New School look back not only to 1776, but also to another anniversary moment: 1926, the year of the American sesquicentennial.The 150th anniversary unfolded in the shadow of World War I, the Red Scare, the consolidation of modern mass media, the rise of expert administration, and the restrictive Immigration Act of 1924. Taking the so-called “Lippmann-Dewey debate” as one point of departure, this panel considers how debates over democracy, public opinion, expertise, media, and political belonging in the 1920s can illuminate the unresolved questions of American democracy today.How is public knowledge produced? What role should experts, journalists, universities, and civic institutions play in democratic life? Who belongs to “the people” or “the public”? And what would it mean to imagine the American public as dynamic and unfinished?

events.name: Sextech Screening Series: Atlantics (2019) in Conversation with Prof. David Bering-Porter
events.venue: The New School - Kellen Auditorium, Room N101, Shelia C. Johnson Design Center
events.description: Join us for a screening of the film Atlantics (2019; dir. Mati Diop), followed by a conversation with David Bering-Porter, PhD. Light refreshments will be served.  About the Film In a popular suburb of Dakar, workers on the construction site of a futuristic tower, without pay for months, decide to leave the country by the ocean for a better future. Among them is Souleiman, the lover of Ada, promised to another. About David Bering-Porter David Bering-Porter is Associate Professor of Culture and Media at the Eugene Lang College of the Liberal Arts at The New School, where his research and teaching address film and media studies, digital culture, and the intersections of Black studies and artificial intelligence. His first book, Undead Labor: Capitalism's Zombie Workers (University of Minnesota Press, 2026), traces the figure of the zombie from Haitian revolutionary culture to contemporary automation discourse, showing how race, labor, and value converge in the mediated body of the undead worker. He is currently at work on a second book, Digital Doppelgänger: The Second Life of Living Labor, which extends that inquiry into voice cloning, generative avatars, and other AI systems built to replicate human behavior. His writing has appeared in Critical Inquiry, Post45, Culture Machine, MIRAJ, Flow, Calibano, and the Los Angeles Review of Books.  About the Screening Series Presented by SexTech Lab in collaboration with the Philosophy Film Club and Ruff Cuts, the screening series is an interdepartmental, cross-disciplinary initiative that engages with film as an intellectual and cultural work to be discussed, debated, and thought with. The series draws on New York City’s extraordinary density of critics, journalists, artists, filmmakers, and public scholars in our orbit, bringing them into dialogue with internal experts at The New School, moderated by students across departments and programs. Each event pairs a screening with dialogue that approaches cinema through historical, philosophical, political, and psychological lenses, showing how public debate, academic inquiry, and applied industry insight can sharpen one another.

events.name: Sandbox Percussion performs John Luther Adams’s Prophecies of Fire.
events.description: Experience John Luther Adams’s Prophecies of Fire, which had its world premiere by Sandbox Percussion in 2024 and makes its New York premiere at The New School.ABOUT PROPHECIES OF FIRE...and I come back to findthe stars misplaced,and the smell of a world that has burned.—Jimi HendrixMy earliest musical awakening was as a drummer. From rock bands to playing timpani in a symphony orchestra, my deepest physical connections to music have been through percussion. Over the past five decades, my life’s work has led me to compose music for orchestra, string quartet, human voices, piano, electronics, and a wide variety of other media. Now, in my 70s, I’ve returned to the place where I began.Prophecies of Fire is a perpetual acceleration canon —unbroken streams of rhythm inexorably rising in pitch and growing brighter, always seeming to get faster while never quite arriving. The musicians should surround the listeners, enveloping them in a maelstrom of tones and timbres, dynamics and velocities —like the wildfires and superstorms, the turbulent seas and waves of heat now rising all around the earth. But beyond any metaphorical associations, Prophecies of Fire is a celebration of the elemental power of sound itself to touch, to move, and perhaps even to transform human consciousness.— John Luther AdamsABOUT JOHN LUTHER ADAMSFor almost forty years, John Luther Adams made his home in the boreal forest of interior Alaska, where he discovered a unique musical world grounded in space, stillness, and elemental forces.In the 1970s and into the ’80s, JLA worked full-time as an environmental activist. But the time came when he felt compelled to dedicate himself entirely to music. He made this choice with the belief that, ultimately, music can do more than politics to change the world. Since that time, he has become one of the most widely admired and influential composers in the world, receiving the Pulitzer Prize, a Grammy Award, and many other honors. In works such as Become Ocean, Become Desert, An Atlas of Deep Time, and Canticles of the Holy Wind, JLA brings the sense of wonder that we feel outdoors into the concert hall. His outdoor works such as Inuksuit, Sila: The Breath of the World, and Crossing Open Ground invite us to remember and reclaim our connections with place, wherever we may be. Now in his 70s, JLA’s deep concern for the state of the earth and the future of humanity drives him to continue composing. As he puts it: “If we can imagine a culture and a society in which we each feel more deeply responsible for our own place in the world, then we just may be able to bring that culture and that society into being.” Since leaving Alaska, JLA and his wife Cynthia have lived in the Sonoran Desert of Mexico, the Atacama Desert of Chile, and the Chihuahuan Desert of New Mexico. They now make their home in the Red Centre of Australia.ABOUT SANDBOX PERCUSSIONDescribed as “exhilarating” by The New York Times and “utterly mesmerizing” by The Guardian, the GRAMMY®-nominated ensemble Sandbox Percussion champions living composers through its unwavering dedication to contemporary chamber music. In 2011, Jonathan Allen, Victor Caccese, Ian Rosenbaum, and Terry Sweeney were brought together by their love of chamber music and the simple joy of playing together; they have since captivated audiences with performances that are both visually and aurally stunning. In 2024, Sandbox Percussion became the first percussion ensemble to be awarded the prestigious Avery Fisher Career Grant.

events.name: Design and Technology Cloud Salon: Colleen Macklin
events.venue: The New School - Kellen Auditorium - Room 101
events.description: Colleen Macklin is a game designer and a Professor in the school of Art, Media and Technology at Parsons School of Design. She’s interested in how games model and reveal ideologies through systems. At Parsons, she is the founder and co-director of PETLab, a design research lab that develops games for experimental learning and social engagement. PETLab projects include disaster preparedness games and sports with the Red Cross, the urban activist game Re:Activism and the physical/fiscal sport Budgetball. She is a member of the game design collective Local No. 12, known for the videogame Dear Reader and the social card game, The Metagame. She has co-authored (with John Sharp) Games, Design and Play: A detailed look at iterative game design (Addison Wesley Professional, 2016) and Iterate: Ten Lessons in Design and Failure (MIT Press, 2019). Colleen has a BFA in Media Arts from Pratt Institute, and an MA in International Affairs from The New School.The Design and Technology programs at Parsons present Cloud Salon, a lecture series that invites artists, designers, technologists, and industry professionals to present projects and to engage in direct conversations with participants. This semester Cloud Salon will focus on featuring full-time faculty at The New School with a creative practice at the intersection of Design and Technology.

events.name: Book Launch: On Un/Certainty by Natasha Lennard, In Conversation with Alice Crary
events.venue: The New School - 66 West 12th Street, New York, NY, Room A-407
events.description: Please join The New School's Natasha Lennard and Alice Crary for a discussion of Natasha's new book, On Un/Certainty: The Uses of Doubt in Dangerous Times.About On Un/Certainty:While politicians, CEOs, and pundits reflexively invoke “uncertain times” to explain everything from pandemic responses, to AI-industry depredations, to climate inaction, and more, journalist and theorist Natasha Lennard offers a radical intervention. Drawing on the philosophy of Ludwig Wittgenstein and placing his work alongside thinkers rarely put into conversation, Lennard demonstrates how our obsession with uncertainty masks the violent certainties that dominate our fracturing world. On Un/Certainty applies philosophical insight to political practice, offering readers not just analysis but hope—and conceptual tools with which to act."An invitation to rethink what we know, and how we know it. Lennard challenges conventional understandings of crisis, borders and gender, revealing how deeply entrenched certainties shape our perceptions of the world."—Naomi Klein, author of Doppelganger"On Un/Certainty seeks to name and so unseat 'pernicious certainty in action,' and call for a different paradigm around the truths we take for granted–specifically as they pertain to what pundits are calling the polycrisis...Lennard’s got a knack for making the heady feel approachable, even to a layperson. This promises to be a most topical intervention for the thinking human. (Bonus: it’s slim enough to take on the subway.)" —Most Anticipated Books of 2026,  Lit Hub"For penetrating and revolutionary insights, not only into 'the news' per se but also into our hell-world’s basic epistemic workings and (especially) their impermanency, I always look to Natasha Lennard. At the same time as demonstrating almost every day—for well over a decade now—what a precious thing journalism can still be, Lennard has become this century’s most illuminating political reader of Wittgenstein and our most invigorating public philosopher of antifascism." —Sophie Lewis, author of Femmephilia

events.name: Fascism, Populism, and Red Pill Politics: Or Why So Many Workers Turn from Left to Right
events.venue: The New School - Wolff Conference Room Albert and Vera List Academic Center, room D1103 6 East 16th Street
events.description: What actually is the relationship between yesterday’s fascism and today’s right-wing populism? In his new, strikingly book, Red Pill Politics: Demystifying Today's Far Right From Fascism to Right-Wing Populism, David Ost argues that these are but two versions of a similar kind of politics that emerges during tough economic times when the Left offers no alternative and its ties to the working class weaken. Using examples from contemporary America, Europe, and Asia and from Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany, Ost explains why the Red Pill radical right is able to win the support of non-elites who traditionally align with the Left, and shows what the broad Left has done historically, and can do today, to defeat it.

events.name: Sites of Memory, Spaces of Resistance: Doing Decolonial Public History in Puerto Rico
events.venue: The New School - Wolff Conference Room
events.description: Who decides what is worth remembering? Whose memory becomes the memory of the nation? Through its engagement with public history, Memoria (De)colonial, an educational organization based in Puerto Rico, addresses these questions by interrogating the colonial legacies embedded in commemorative sites and examining how they shape collective memory and historical narratives. Through digital and public humanities initiatives, the project democratizes knowledge production by fostering spaces for participatory engagement, critical reflection, and decolonial pedagogy.In this event, Memoria (De)colonial presents its public memory initiatives and discusses the transformative potential of public humanities as a decolonial intervention. In particular, they share their project, (Des)vío/(De)tours. This public history program uses monuments, art, and heritage sites as entry points to examine and contest the colonial narratives embedded in Puerto Rico’s public spaces and curricula. By reimagining these spaces as sites of dialogue, resistance, and collective meaning-making, (Des)vío/(De)tours fosters critical engagement with dominant historical narratives and envisions public spaces as sites of liberation, healing, and reparation.Following presentations by Dr. Rafael Capó Garcia (Founder and Director of Memoria (De)colonial) and Sofía Martínez Rivera (Director of the (Des)vío/(De)tours program), Dr. Eduardo Rivera Pichardo and Gabriel Pita Colón (Research Collaborator at the University of Puerto Rico) will introduce a collaborative longitudinal study scheduled to launch in early 2027. The social psychological study examines how these decolonial interventions reshape collective memories, foster critical consciousness, and catalyze political action over time. Engagement with the audience, questions, interventions, and a general reception will follow.

events.name: Selected Papers of the 14th International Sándor Ferenczi Conference
events.description: with presentations by: Jô Gondar, PhDDaniel Kupermann, PhDEugênio Canesin Dal Molin, PhDJudy Eekhoff, PhDEndre Koritar, MD The title of the 2024 São Paulo Sándor Ferenczi Conference was “Psychoanalysis between Catastrophe and Creation: Emerging Perspectives.” The São Paulo Conference, a highly successful event, brought together close to 1,000 clinicians, scholars, researchers, students, and experienced colleagues. The SFC is very pleased to bring the presenters from Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Seattle, and Vancouver back together to share their work with our community. The conference tapped into Sándor Ferenczi’s deep understanding of the complex and traumatizing dynamics of power and human vulnerability.  His ongoing progressive work in responding to traumatic experiences in his clinical work, enriched the knowledge of conference participants about disruptive social, personal, political, environmental and clinical situations that we are facing today.The four themes of the conference were: Emerging from Catastrophes: Social and Environmental Transformations The Clinical and the Sociopolitical: Challenges for Psychoanalysis in Times of Trauma Fragmentation and its Consequences on Psychic Life Confusion of Tongues: Tenderness, Trauma and Toxicity Each speaker will touch on these themes in their presentation, detailed below. ***Jô Gondar, PhD: “With Ferenczi for a Decolonial Psychoanalysis” Eugênio Canesin Dal Molin, PhD: “Shock, Resonance, and Creation” Daniel Kupermann, PhD: “The Mongrel Complex: Identification with the Aggressor, Self-Hatred, versus the Resting Drive (Ruhetrieb)” Judy Eekhoff, PhD: “Catastrophe and Creativity: From Fragmentation to Emergence” Endre Koritar, MD: “Mother Tongue and the Language of Tenderness: Lost and Found”***Learning ObjectivesAt the end of the workshop, participants will be able to: 1) Describe the transdisciplinary belief of Ferenczi, that psychoanalysis should be linked to social, political and subjective transformation in each aspect of diverse human experiences.2) Explain the Ferenczian ideas of the dynamics of trauma and its effects on psychic functioning, such as shock and the possible emergence of a creative aspect.3) Understand how the omnipresent effect of subjectivation in societal power relations, and in individual lives, the disavowal of trauma, the unthinkable, the unspeakable and unrepresentable induces the identification with the aggressor, illustrated by the unique Brazilian model of the Mongrel Complex.4) Utilize the importance of Ferenczi’s emphasis on honesty in relationships, the honest emotional link between patient and analyst that occurs first and foremost on a somatic level, how catastrophic change can be either creative or fragmenting depending on whether the emotional tie (familial or therapeutic) to the other is based on truth or lies. 5) Assess the impact of early catastrophic experiences in a young person’s life, worsened by his family’s subsequent immigration, solidifying his feelings of isolation and deadness, and how he benefited from treatment.

events.name: Marketing Radicalism
events.venue: The New School - Wolff Conference Room
events.description: The Center for the American Experience in collaboration with The New School Department of Sociology is proud to present the launch of Professor Virág Molnár's new book, Marketing Radicalism: The Cultural Production of Far-Right Populism in Contemporary Hungary (Princeton University Press). Join us for an inspiring night of conversation between Professor Molnár and Heuss Visiting Professor in Sociology Professor Manuela Boatcǎ on this new book and its timely significance in America, with an introduction from CAE co-director Professor Julia Sonnevend.  Attacks on iconic public institutions such as the Kennedy Center or the Smithsonian, political interventions into university curricula, book bans curbing free speech in public schools, expanding restrictions on LGBTQ+ and Transgender rights, and dismantling of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion policies illustrate the political centrality of culture wars in the Trump era.  Marketing Radicalism is a book that promises new insights into such struggles, as it moves away from a focus on political parties and electoral politics to highlighting the significance of culture wars, identity politics, culture industries and popular culture in the rise of far-right populism. Looking at such domains as fashion, book publishing, tourism and martial arts, the book shows how the culture industries create powerful narratives to reimagine the nation as a populist fantasyland, and how these narratives are used by far-right governments in their efforts to topple liberal norms.  While Marketing Radicalism focuses on Hungary under Viktor Orbán, it emphasizes how Orbán provided an ideological blueprint for far-right populist politicians – and a cautionary tale for liberal democracies. It offers important lessons on the mainstreaming of right-wing popular culture, the importance of markets in circulating far-right identity narratives, and the political mobilization of cultural traditions for geopolitical reorientation.

events.name: Why can't our universities be free? Higher Education, Financialization and Workers' Strugg
events.venue: The New School - Starr Hall 63 Fifth Avenue, UL#105
events.description: Higher education in the US and beyond is under attack. The potential of universities to act as sanctuaries of dissent is directly undermined both by the neoliberal "restructuring" of academic institutions and by external government pressure to control and suppress dissident thought. At the same time, the mass mobilization of students, student-workers, faculty, and staff around labor rights, academic freedom, justice, and peace across the globe has once again illuminated the importance of maintaining higher education as a progressive space for critical thinking and organizing. The workers' struggle at The New School expresses many of these tensions, prompting us to ask "why can't our universities be free" and to reflect on what is required to fight back.In this hybrid event organized by the Series of Advanced Political Economy, Professor of Economics Sanjay Reddy, Professor Emeritus of Economics Richard Wolff, and ACT-UAW Local 7902 President Micaela Suminski join us for a discussion moderated by PhD Economics student Danielle Twiss.About SAPE:Sape is a joint program organized by the Economics Departments at SOAS University of London, The New School for Social Research, and the Free Institute.We launched the Series in 2022 to promote political economy beyond university walls and created a platform where academics, activists, trade unionists, and many others could come together to discuss pressing issues and explore ways to address the multi-faceted crises of our time. As of today, these lectures have collectively gained thousands of views on YouTube, in addition to the live in-person and Zoom webinar attendees.Our series has been part of the General Federation of Trade Unions (GFTU) UK, through the UK government-funded Knowledge Transfer Partnership project. With this project, we aim to connect the academic and theoretical discussions in the lecture series with workers’ struggles in the UK and internationally. The objective is to reach a wider audience, particularly the union members, leaders, and shop stewards through the GFTU’s broad network of trade unions. Our goal is to equip workers with the tools necessary for understanding macroeconomic policies and the political economy of decision-making in contemporary capitalist society. Please register to secure your seat.

events.description: FutureWorks is the BBA’s annual open house, bringing students, faculty, alumni, and industry professionals together around works-in-progress by students from Parsons’ BBA Strategic Design & Management program.Explore emerging student research and discoveries, meet the talented designers behind the work, discuss the questions they’re exploring, and be inspired by the opportunities they make possible.Then join us for good food and even better conversation with the next generation of designers, question-askers, and future-finders.About the BBA Strategic Design & Management:The BBA Strategic Design & Management program at Parsons School of Design offers a world-class business degree from the #1 design school in the country. We prepare emerging designers to take on wicked problems that cross industries, geographies, disciplines, ideologies, and communities. We help students understand that all problems exist within dynamic contexts and systems and that responsible action requires learning from and designing with diverse stakeholders, not just shareholders.Our students, who come from all over the world, learn to match design thinking to design doing, to think both logically and associatively, to visualize their discoveries, to present and communicate in compelling ways, and to be critical and deliberate in how they choose to respond to today’s challenges and opportunities. In their time at Parsons, they also take courses in branding, design history, product and service development, innovation, law, finance, ethics, and team dynamics.

events.name: Cybernetics Then and Now: Lectures on Music and Technology
events.venue: The New School - Wollman Hall, 65 W 11th St, New York, NY 10011
events.description: The scientific engineering of feedback between humans and technology, composers and machines, has pushed the field of electroacoustic music since its origins in European radio studios. A pair of lectures by Theodore Gordon and Kari Watson reminds us how these relationships continue to shape the contemporary experimental music landscape. Together, the lectures connect a selection of works performed during the Darmstadt at 80 Festival, including Stockhausen’s Kontakte (1958–60), Herbert Brün’s Mutatis Mutandis (1968), Angharad Davies’ Empty Spaces II (2023), the New York premiere of Anthony Braxton’s Thunder Music (2023), and Watson’s own work, Fuse (2026). The event will also feature a performance by electric guitarist Yaron Deutsch and be moderated by part-time faculty member, Nick Hallett. Theodore Gordon: Cybernetic Transparency, Cybernetic OpacityKari Watson: In Search of Seams. Cyborg Emergence in My Recent Work Yaron Deutsch is an Israeli guitarist, improviser, and artistic director of Ensemble Nikel, which he co-founded in 2006 with saxophonist Gan Lev. Known for his work in contemporary and experimental music, Deutsch has collaborated extensively with leading composers including Michael Beil, Pierluigi Billone, Raphaël Cendo, Chaya Czernowin, Philippe Hurel, Stefan Prins, and Michael Wertmüller, premiering new works as both soloist and ensemble musician. A frequent guest performer with Klangforum Wien, he has also appeared with Ensemble musikFabrik, Ensemble Ictus, the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra, and major European orchestras under conductors including Peter Eötvös and Zubin Mehta. Deutsch is regularly on the faculty of Darmstadt Summer Course. Presented by the Contemporary Music Program within the Arts Department at Eugene Lang College of Liberal Arts at The New School. Organized by Nick Hallett and Zach Layton, curators of NYC’s Darmstadt: Classics of the Avant-Garde, together with Thomas Schäfer, director of the Internationales Musikinstitut Darmstadt, and George Lewis, Artistic Director of the International Contemporary Ensemble, the festival bridges generations of experimental sound. Envisioned in partnership with a consortium including Roulette Intermedium, The New School, Fridman Gallery, International Contemporary Ensemble, Ramapo College, and the Goethe-Institut.

events.description: Watch giant character balloons come to life the afternoon before the parade around the Museum of Natural History (77th to 81st St).

events.name: 100th Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
events.venue: Upper West Side to Herald Square (6th Ave)
events.description: The historic 100th anniversary of Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, stepping off at 77th & Central Park West down to 34th St.

events.name: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony
events.description: Live musical performances and the ceremonial lighting of the world-famous Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree.

events.name: Times Square New Year's Eve Ball Drop & Celebration
events.description: The global New Year's Eve celebration featuring live star performances, commercial hourly countdowns, and the midnight crystal ball drop.

events.name: Lunar New Year Chinatown Firecracker Ceremony & Cultural Festival
events.description: Traditional firecrackers to ward off evil spirits, lion dance troupes, martial arts, and cultural performances welcoming the New Year.

events.name: 266th New York City St. Patrick's Day Parade
events.description: The world's oldest and largest civilian parade, marching up Fifth Avenue past St. Patrick's Cathedral with bands, bagpipes, and Irish societies.

events.name: Museum Mile Festival 2027
events.description: Fifth Avenue is closed to traffic for 28 blocks as 8 world-class museums (The Met, Guggenheim, Cooper Hewitt, El Museo, etc.) open free to the public.

events.name: 45th Annual Coney Island Mermaid Parade
events.description: The nation's largest art parade celebrating marine mythology and artistic self-expression on the historic Coney Island Boardwalk.

events.name: NYC Pride March 2027
events.description: The monumental annual civil rights march from 25th St down 5th Ave past the Stonewall National Monument to 16th St.
